source.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array

teaching.hint: How does one unpaired element change the positions occupied by all pairs after it?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Before the singleton, pairs start at even indices; after it, their alignment shifts to odd indices.
solution_outline.approach: Binary-search the singleton’s interval using an even-aligned midpoint. Equal adjacent values at that midpoint let the search skip that complete pair; unequal values keep the midpoint and the earlier half.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The singleton remains inside the interval. Equal-pair alignment at even indices holds strictly before it and fails at or after it.
solution_outline.correctness: The singleton index is even because preceding values occupy complete pairs. At an even midpoint before it, that value and the next are its pair; at or beyond it, the singleton or shifted alignment makes them unequal. Each branch retains exactly the possible side and shrinks the interval until the singleton is its only index.
solution_outline.pitfall: A whole-array XOR scan violates the explicit logarithmic bound; ensure an adjacent comparison is in range.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained sortedness, exact multiplicities, value bounds, and mandatory time/space requirements.
common_wrong_turns: A whole-array XOR scan violates the explicit logarithmic bound; ensure an adjacent comparison is in range.
